subject: Transactional latency spikes — request to discuss remediation, credits, and premium onramp
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@fastpay.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@fastpay.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Transactional latency spikes impacting checkout - ask for remediation and credits

Aisha,

We saw another set of latency spikes overnight in our transactional path (payment authorization calls). Our engineering team captured a few 95th/99th percentile bursts around 1.3-1.8s for simple generation requests — up from our normal ~200-300ms. This is causing checkout retries and a measurable drop in conversion on peak traffic.

We need to understand:
- What caused the spikes?
- What guarantees can Redwood provide while we evaluate options (dedicated pool / premium tier)?
- Can we get a short-term credit for the impact window while we decide on a remediation path?

Attached is a short CSV with example request ids, timestamps, and latency values. We'd like to schedule a 30-min call today to walk through telemetry and next steps.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Engineering — FastPay

Attachment: fastpay-2026-08-latency-sample.csv
From: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fastpay.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@fastpay.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Transactional latency spikes impacting checkout - ask for remediation and credits

Samir — thanks for the data and flagging this. Deeply sorry for the impact.

Short answers up front:
- We're treating this as priority and will open an incident review with the infra team now.
- We can propose a short remediation plan (routing/pinning + temporary dedicated capacity) and a one-time credit tied to the observed impact window.
- If you want sustained tail protection we can outline the Premium SLA path (lower latency SLO, regional redundancy, 24/7 priority on-call) and a migration/pricing plan.

I can be on a call today at 2:00pm ET — does that work for you and Elena? I'll bring Neha (infra lead) and Marissa (customer success) for the remediation/contract discussion.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — developer-first LLM inference
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Transactional latency spikes - preliminary technical notes (internal)

Aisha / Marissa — quick internal notes before the call:

Observations from infra (prelim):
- Spike pattern matches a short-lived KV cache eviction sequence when request fanout exceeded our batch-window heuristic during a traffic surge. We saw cache misses aligned with 99th spikes.
- Hypothesis: a request pattern with high prefix variance triggered batching/path selection that reverted to a slower kernel path for some replicas.

Mitigations we can propose on the call (low friction -> higher impact):
1) Short-term: pin FastPay traffic to a warm pool with forced KV prewarming + disable aggressive batching for 24-72h (should drop 99th by ~500-800ms in our tests).
2) Medium: provision a small Dedicated pool for transactional endpoints (reserved capacity + single-tenant isolation).
3) Long-term: tune kernel-selection heuristics for their workload and offer a quantization/profile that reduces tail variance.

Costs & timeline (rough):
- Short-term warm-pool + config change: 24h to enact, minimal cost (small hourly premium).
- Dedicated mini-pool (2 GPUs): 7-10 days to provision and test; monthly commitment.

I'll join the call and can prepare simple before/after latency curves.

-Neha
Director, Serving Infrastructure
From: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fastpay.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@fastpay.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Transactional latency spikes impacting checkout - proposed remediation & credit

Samir / Elena — thanks for the quick sync. Summary and proposed path:

What we observed: short KV-cache eviction cascades that elevated 95th/99th tail for ~45 minutes during your 03:10-04:00 UTC window.

Immediate remediation (we can enact within 24 hours):
- Pin transactional routes to a warm pool and prewarm KV (24-72h stabilization window).
- Disable aggressive continuous-batching for those routes for the immediate window.

Commercial/credits proposal:
- One-time goodwill credit of 7% of the invoice for the impacted billing period, conditioned on acceptance of the short-term remedy and a 3-month telemetry review.

Premium/upgrade path (if FastPay wants a sustained guarantee):
- Offer: Premium Availability Tier (SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for transactional routes; reduced 95th/99th latency SLOs; priority capacity and regional failover).
- Onramp: 2-week pilot on a small Dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent nodes), then conversion to a monthly reserved commitment.
- Estimated delta: +18-24% on current recurring spend, depending on peak capacity. Exact quote after sizing call.

Next steps:
1) Do you accept the short-term action so we can schedule the warm pool change?
2) If you want to pursue Premium, we can circulate a proposed SLA amendment and Pilot Statement of Work (SOW).

I'll prepare the draft SLA amendment and attach it here.

Best,
Aisha

Attachment: redwood-proposed-sla-amendment-v1.pdf
From: Samir Khan <samir@fastpay.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@fastpay.com>, FastPay Procurement <procurement@fastpay.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Transactional latency spikes impacting checkout - proposed remediation & credit

Aisha — thank you and team for the concrete plan. FastPay accepts the short-term remediation (please schedule the warm pool + batching disable this week).

Regarding the credit: procurement will review the 7% goodwill credit against the impacted invoice period. Procurement is also open to the Premium path, but we need the draft SLA amendment and a clear pilot SOW that includes success criteria and rollback conditions. Elena and procurement want guaranteed rollback if pilot increases error-rate or cost without latency improvements.

Please route the SLA amendment and SOW to procurement@fastpay.com and I'll coordinate internal approvals. Also include a simple comparison table: current plan vs proposed premium (latency SLOs, regional redundancy, on-call response).

Samir
Director of Engineering — FastPay
